accepted.s: Who captured Ahmadnagar city and Asirgarh respectively in 1600 and 1601?
accepted.x: Akbar captured Ahmadnagar city in 1600 and Asirgarh of Khandesh in 1601.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–conquest association to eliminate rulers connected with later Deccan campaigns.
accepted.sec: Annexation of Deccan Sultanates by the Mughals - rulers, fate of the last rulers

accepted.s: The Nizam Shahi dynasty of Ahmadnagar was ended during the reign of
accepted.x: Shah Jahan ended the Nizam Shahis in 1633.
accepted.tq: Match the dynasty’s termination with the correct Mughal ruler and period.
accepted.sec: Annexation of Deccan Sultanates by the Mughals - rulers, fate of the last rulers

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the relationship between Bijapur, Golconda and Shah Jahan:
1. Bijapur and Golconda accepted Mughal suzerainty in 1636.
2. They agreed to pay an indemnity.
3. Golconda’s Inqiyad Nama provided for a tribute of two lakh hun.
4. The khutba in Golconda was to be read in Shah Jahan’s name.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The 1636 agreements involved suzerainty, indemnity, a two-lakh-hun tribute from Golconda and the khutba in Shah Jahan’s name.
accepted.tq: Check whether all details in the diplomatic settlement belong to the same 1636 agreement.
accepted.sec: Annexation of Deccan Sultanates by the Mughals - rulers, fate of the last rulers

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Annexation of Bijapur by Aurangzeb
B. Ahmadnagar city captured by Akbar
C. Golconda annexed as the 21st Mughal Suba
D. Nizam Shahi dynasty ended by Shah Jahan
accepted.x: The correct order is Ahmadnagar’s capture in 1600, the end of the Nizam Shahis in 1633, Bijapur’s annexation in 1686 and Golconda’s annexation in 1687.
accepted.tq: Place the events by their dates before comparing the middle positions.
accepted.sec: Annexation of Deccan Sultanates by the Mughals - rulers, fate of the last rulers

accepted.s: Who opened the gates of Golconda Fort to Aurangzeb on 21 September 1687?
accepted.x: The gates were opened by the traitor Abdullah Khan Pani, also referred to as Abdullah Phani in the accounts.
accepted.tq: Use the person–deed trap by associating the gate-opening with the named traitor rather than the defender.
accepted.sec: Annexation of Deccan Sultanates by the Mughals - rulers, fate of the last rulers

accepted.s: Golconda was annexed to the Mughal Empire on
accepted.x: Golconda was annexed on 3 October 1687 and became the twenty-first Suba of the Mughal Empire.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of the gates being opened from the later date of annexation.
accepted.sec: Annexation of Deccan Sultanates by the Mughals - rulers, fate of the last rulers

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Abul Hasan Tana Shah is correct?
o: He was imprisoned at Daulatabad and died there in 1699.
He escaped to Bijapur after the fall of Golconda.
He died at Bidar after being imprisoned there throughout his life.
He was executed at Golconda in 1687.
accepted.x: The last Qutb Shahi ruler, Abul Hasan Tana Shah, was imprisoned first at Bidar and then at Daulatabad, where he died in 1699.
accepted.tq: Separate the place of imprisonment from the place of death in a fate-of-the-ruler question.
accepted.sec: Annexation of Deccan Sultanates by the Mughals - rulers, fate of the last rulers

accepted.s: Abul Razak Lari was honoured for
o: negotiating the 1636 treaty with Shah Jahan
accepted.x: Abul Razak Lari was honoured for his defence of Golconda during the Mughal siege.
accepted.tq: Match the military personality with the specific deed for which he was honoured.
accepted.sec: Annexation of Deccan Sultanates by the Mughals - rulers, fate of the last rulers

accepted.s: Which of the following places was NOT among the territories conquered by Sultan Quli?
accepted.x: Sultan Quli conquered Rachakonda, Devarakonda and Rajahmundry, among other places. Kondavidu was gained by Ibrahim after 1565.
accepted.tq: Find the place associated with Ibrahim’s later coastal expansion rather than Sultan Quli’s conquests.
accepted.sec: Golconda and Andhra - coastal conquests, Telugu patronage (Malkibharama), Akkanna-Madanna

accepted.s: Which of the following sets contains only territories associated with Sultan Quli’s conquests?
accepted.x: Sultan Quli took Rachakonda, Devarakonda, Warangal, Rajahmundry, Eluru and Kovilakonda. Kondavidu and Machilipatnam were gained by Ibrahim after 1565.
accepted.tq: Group the places by ruler before selecting the set with no later Ibrahim conquest.
accepted.sec: Golconda and Andhra - coastal conquests, Telugu patronage (Malkibharama), Akkanna-Madanna

accepted.s: After 1565, Ibrahim Qutb Shah’s acquisition of Kondavidu and Machilipatnam led to the annexation of coastal Andhra during
accepted.x: Ibrahim gained Kondavidu and Machilipatnam after 1565, and coastal Andhra was annexed during 1570–1578.
accepted.tq: Use the sequence ‘after 1565’ and the specific date range to reject nearby periods.
accepted.sec: Golconda and Andhra - coastal conquests, Telugu patronage (Malkibharama), Akkanna-Madanna

accepted.s: Ibrahim Qutb Shah was referred to as ‘Malkibharama’ by
accepted.x: Telugu poets called Ibrahim Qutb Shah ‘Malkibharama’.
accepted.tq: Identify the cultural group associated with the title rather than the ruler’s political opponents.
accepted.sec: Golconda and Andhra - coastal conquests, Telugu patronage (Malkibharama), Akkanna-Madanna

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Poet)
a. Addanki Gangadhara
b. Ponnaganti Telaganarya
c. Kandukuri Rudrakavi
List-II (Work)
i. Sugriva Vijayam
ii. Yayati Charitra

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Addanki Gangadhara wrote Tapati Samvaranopakhyanamu, Ponnaganti Telaganarya wrote Yayati Charitra, and Kandukuri Rudrakavi wrote Sugriva Vijayam.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure poet–work pair and complete the remaining matches by elimination.

accepted.s: Which work is regarded as the first Telugu poem or kavya dedicated to a Muslim ruler?
accepted.x: Addanki Gangadhara’s Tapati Samvaranopakhyanamu is regarded as the first Telugu poem or kavya dedicated to a Muslim ruler.
accepted.tq: Match the literary distinction with the correct title rather than with the author alone.
accepted.sec: Golconda and Andhra - coastal conquests, Telugu patronage (Malkibharama), Akkanna-Madanna

accepted.s: Ponnaganti Telaganarya’s Yayati Charitra is notable as
o: the first Telugu work on revenue administration
the first Telugu poem written under Abul Hasan
the first kavya in pure Telugu
accepted.x: Yayati Charitra is identified as the first kavya in pure Telugu. Its dedication is attributed to Amir Khan in one account and to Ibrahim in another.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the work’s literary distinction from its disputed dedication.
accepted.sec: Golconda and Andhra - coastal conquests, Telugu patronage (Malkibharama), Akkanna-Madanna

accepted.s: Who wrote Sugriva Vijayam, regarded as the first Telugu Yakshagana?
accepted.x: Kandukuri Rudrakavi wrote Sugriva Vijayam, regarded as the first Telugu Yakshagana.
accepted.tq: Use the literary form–author association to distinguish Rudrakavi from the other court poets.
accepted.sec: Golconda and Andhra - coastal conquests, Telugu patronage (Malkibharama), Akkanna-Madanna

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Kandukuri Rudrakavi:
1. He wrote Sugriva Vijayam.
2. He wrote Nirankusopakhyanam.
3. He wrote Janardanashtakam.
4. He received the Rentachintala agraharam.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct according to the standard attribution of these works and the recorded grant of Rentachintala agraharam to Rudrakavi.
accepted.tq: Verify the complete author–works–patronage cluster before choosing the inclusive combination.
accepted.sec: Golconda and Andhra - coastal conquests, Telugu patronage (Malkibharama), Akkanna-Madanna

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Movva padams are associated with Kshetrayya. Akkanna was a military official, not the composer associated with those padams.
accepted.tq: Find the mismatched person–work association among closely related Golconda personalities.
accepted.sec: Golconda and Andhra - coastal conquests, Telugu patronage (Malkibharama), Akkanna-Madanna

accepted.s: Kshetrayya and Bhakta Ramadasu were associated respectively with the courts of
accepted.x: Kshetrayya was associated with Abdullah’s court, while Bhakta Ramadasu, or Kancherla Gopanna, was associated with Abul Hasan’s court.
accepted.tq: Separate similar court associations by matching each cultural figure to his patron.
accepted.sec: Golconda and Andhra - coastal conquests, Telugu patronage (Malkibharama), Akkanna-Madanna

accepted.s: Chand Bibi was the daughter of
accepted.x: Chand Bibi was the daughter of Hussain Nizam Shah I of Ahmadnagar.
accepted.tq: Use the family relationship rather than the marital alliance to identify Chand Bibi’s parentage.

accepted.s: Chand Bibi’s marriage to Ali Adil Shah of Bijapur helped to
o: end the Nizam Shahi dynasty in 1595
create the first revenue-farming system in Ahmadnagar
accepted.x: Her marriage to Ali Adil Shah of Bijapur sealed the anti-Vijayanagara alliance.
accepted.tq: Connect a dynastic marriage with its immediate political consequence.
accepted.sec: Ahmednagar - Chand Bibi, Malik Ambar's revenue system

accepted.s: Chand Bibi defended Ahmadnagar against the Mughals during
accepted.x: Chand Bibi defended Ahmadnagar against the Mughals in 1595–1596. Ahmadnagar fell in 1600, when she died.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the period of defence from the later year of Ahmadnagar’s fall.
accepted.sec: Ahmednagar - Chand Bibi, Malik Ambar's revenue system

accepted.s: Who was the Abyssinian regent of the Nizam Shahis who resisted Jahangir?
accepted.x: Malik Ambar was an Abyssinian regent of the Nizam Shahis and resisted the Mughal emperor Jahangir.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive identity and political role with the correct Deccan administrator.
accepted.sec: Ahmednagar - Chand Bibi, Malik Ambar's revenue system

accepted.s:
Which of the following features belonged to Malik Ambar’s revenue system?
1. Survey of land
2. Fixed assessment
3. Absence of revenue farming
4. Use of Maratha guerrilla cavalry
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Malik Ambar revived revenue administration on Todar Mal’s lines through survey and fixed assessment, avoided revenue farming and used Maratha guerrilla cavalry.
accepted.tq: Test whether administrative and military innovations are both included in the same reform profile.
accepted.sec: Ahmednagar - Chand Bibi, Malik Ambar's revenue system

accepted.s: Malik Ambar founded Khirki, which later came to be known as
accepted.x: Malik Ambar founded Khirki, which was later known as Aurangabad.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original and later names of the city from nearby Deccan centres.
accepted.sec: Ahmednagar - Chand Bibi, Malik Ambar's revenue system

accepted.s: Who made peace with the Mughals after Malik Ambar’s period?
accepted.x: Fath Khan, Malik Ambar’s son, made peace with the Mughals.
accepted.tq: Use the father–son succession relationship to identify the later negotiator.
accepted.sec: Ahmednagar - Chand Bibi, Malik Ambar's revenue system

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the chief source of state income in the Deccan polity described?
accepted.x: Land revenue was the chief source of income. Leased diamond mines were also described as the highest single source of revenue.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the general chief source from a particularly high individual source.
accepted.sec: Revenue - main source and revenue farming

accepted.s: The leased diamond mines were described as the state’s
accepted.x: The leased diamond mines were called the highest single source, whereas land revenue was the chief general source of income.
accepted.tq: Separate the comparative superlative ‘highest single source’ from the broader ‘chief source’.
accepted.sec: Revenue - main source and revenue farming

accepted.s: The two categories of land mentioned in the revenue system were
accepted.x: Land was classified as Zamindari land and Haveli or crown land.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact paired classification instead of substituting familiar land-revenue terms from other systems.
accepted.sec: Revenue - main source and revenue farming

accepted.s: Dasabandhu lands paid land revenue at the rate of
accepted.x: Dasabandhu lands paid only one-tenth of the produce or assessment as revenue.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact fractional assessment rather than inferring it from the land category.

accepted.s: In the revenue-farming system, collection rights were
accepted.x: The rights to collect revenue were auctioned to the highest bidder.
accepted.tq: Identify the defining operational feature of revenue farming—auction of collection rights.
accepted.sec: Revenue - main source and revenue farming

accepted.s: The bidders who obtained revenue-collection rights were known as
accepted.x: The bidders in the revenue-farming auctions were called Mustajirs and were mostly Hindus.
accepted.tq: Match the technical administrative term with the function it denotes.
accepted.sec: Revenue - main source and revenue farming

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about revenue farming is correct?
o: Mustajirs were hereditary village priests appointed by the Sultan.
Mustajirs collected only customs duties from coastal ports.
Mustajirs were mostly foreign military officers and paid no fixed amount.
Mustajirs were mostly Hindus who secured collection rights through auction.
accepted.x: Mustajirs were mostly Hindus who obtained revenue-collection rights by bidding in auctions.
accepted.tq: Combine the identity of the bidders with the method by which they obtained the rights.
accepted.sec: Revenue - main source and revenue farming

accepted.s: Machilipatnam was leased for revenue collection at
accepted.x: The example given for revenue farming is the lease of Machilipatnam for 1,80,000 pagodas annually.
accepted.tq: Read the place–amount pair carefully and distinguish digit reversal in the options.
accepted.sec: Revenue - main source and revenue farming

accepted.s: Which of the following commodities were state monopolies?
accepted.x: Salt, betel leaf and tobacco were state monopolies.
accepted.tq: Select the complete commodity group rather than a partially correct combination.
accepted.sec: Revenue - main source and revenue farming

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Akkanna and Madanna:
1. They were Pingali Brahmin brothers from Hanamkonda.
2. Madanna served as Mir Jumla or Diwan.
3. Akkanna served as Sar Lashkar.
4. Madanna held the titles Surya Prakasa Rao and Alampana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Madanna was the Diwan or prime minister, while Akkanna was the Sar Lashkar or army chief.
accepted.tq: Check the family, offices and titles together, while avoiding the documented reversal of their roles.
accepted.sec: Madanna and Akkanna - role and fall

accepted.s: Akkanna and Madanna built an alliance with Shivaji in
accepted.x: The brothers built an alliance with Shivaji in 1677.
accepted.tq: Associate the political alliance with its specific year rather than with the later fall of Golconda.
accepted.sec: Madanna and Akkanna - role and fall

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the nephews of Akkanna and Madanna?
o: Podili Linganna — governor of the Karnatak; Gopanna — tahsildar of Palvancha
Podili Linganna — tahsildar of Palvancha; Gopanna — governor of the Karnatak
Podili Linganna — Sar Lashkar; Gopanna — Mir Jumla
Podili Linganna — governor of Golconda; Gopanna — commander of the Karnatak
accepted.x: Podili Linganna was the governor of the Karnatak, while Kancherla Gopanna was the tahsildar of Palvancha.
accepted.tq: Match each nephew with his office, using the distinct administrative locations as clues.
accepted.sec: Madanna and Akkanna - role and fall

accepted.s: The murder of Akkanna and Madanna in 1686 weakened Golconda because it occurred
o: before the Qutb Shahis acquired coastal Andhra
during the establishment of the Nizam Shahi dynasty
immediately after the founding of Khirki
just before the Mughal fall of Golconda
accepted.x: The brothers were murdered in 1686, shortly before Golconda fell to Aurangzeb in 1687, thereby weakening the state’s administration and defence.
accepted.tq: Connect the event’s timing with its political consequence rather than treating it as an isolated date.
accepted.sec: Madanna and Akkanna - role and fall
